title: Six Flags Plans to Open Theme Parks in Saudi Arabia
summary: Six Flags Entertainment Corp. (SIX) announced plans to expand its theme park operations into Saudi Arabia as part of the kingdom's "Vision 2030" reform plan. CEO John Duffey met with Saudi deputy crown prince Mohammed bin Salman to discuss the partnership aimed at boosting entertainment options and diversifying the Saudi economy away from oil revenue. The expansion to Saudi Arabia follows an agreement to open parks in Vietnam and coincides with a regional push to develop theme parks to attract tourists.

title: Mohammed receives Microsoft CEO, discusses smart government services
summary: His Highness Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum met with Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella to discuss the UAE's plans for smart government services and the utilization of advanced technology solutions. The meeting also covered the UAE's National Innovation Strategy and Dubai's innovation strategy. Nadella praised the UAE's development approach and leadership's vision, affirming Microsoft's interest in expanding cooperation.

title: Microsoft Surface Pro 4 finally arrives in India at a starting price of Rs 89,990
summary: Microsoft has officially launched the Surface Pro 4 and the older Surface Pro 3 in India, with the Surface Pro 4 starting at Rs 89,990. The devices are available for pre-order exclusively through Amazon.in, with deliveries commencing from January 14. Microsoft has also established experience centers in major Indian cities for product demonstrations.

title: Gates and Bezos partner with Sloan Kettering for controversial cancer treatment
summary: Bill Gates and Jeff Bezos are partnering with Sloan Kettering to back Grail, a startup focused on detecting cancer. This collaboration comes at a time when technologies like liquid biopsies and gene-sequencing are becoming more affordable and viable for screening at-risk patients. The initiative aims to advance cancer detection methods.

title: Jeff Bezos and Bill Gates bet on blood tests for cancer
summary: Jeff Bezos and Bill Gates have invested in Grail, a startup spun out of Illumina Inc., which aims to detect multiple cancers early through a single blood test. The company announced over $100 million in Series A funding led by Illumina and ARCH Venture Partners, with participation from Bezos Expeditions, Microsoft cofounder Gates, and Sutter Hill Ventures. This venture seeks to revolutionize cancer detection, despite potential profitability challenges.

title: After abandoning iAd revenue, Apple Inc can reintroduce an ad-free internet
summary: Apple's decision to abandon iAd revenue opens the door for a new strategy focused on an ad-free internet, leveraging its strong hardware sales and user ecosystem. The article argues that Apple can starve Google's core advertising business by offering privacy-focused services and content, thereby differentiating itself from ad-supported platforms. This shift capitalizes on the diminishing value of display ads and the increasing demand for high-quality, subscription-based content.

title: Microsoft: Windows 10 will be the only OS supported on new processors
summary: Microsoft announced that Windows 10 will be the only operating system supported on new processor generations from Intel, AMD, NVidia, and Qualcomm. The company urges users and enterprises to upgrade from Windows 7 and 8.1, with support for older OS versions on Skylake devices ending by July 2017. This move aims to ensure security and optimal performance exclusively with Windows 10.

title: Israeli DevOps startup JFrog raises $50m
summary: Israeli DevOps startup JFrog has successfully raised $50 million in a new funding round from several investors including Scale Venture Partners, Sapphire Ventures, and Battery Ventures. These funds will be used for talent acquisition, technological advancements, and global expansion to meet the increasing demand for their DevOps and software automation platform. JFrog, known for its Artifactory and Bintray products, aims to further lead the market with enhanced solutions that are 10x better than single-technology offerings from competitors.

title: IBM, Symantec storage results bode ill for EMC, HPE
summary: Recent fourth-quarter results from IBM's storage business and Symantec's Veritas unit show significant year-over-year revenue declines, painting a bleak picture for the storage market. These negative results suggest potential challenges for industry leaders EMC and Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE), which are expected to report their earnings soon. Despite analysts' expectations for modest growth from EMC, the observed market contraction by IBM and Symantec indicates that EMC might struggle to meet these targets, especially as hardware makers face increasing competition from cloud service providers.

title: Scarlet Mimic: Years-Long Espionage Campaign Targets Minority Activists
summary: Unit 42's investigation reveals "Scarlet Mimic," a sophisticated cyber espionage group active for over four years, primarily targeting minority rights activists, particularly Uyghur and Tibetan individuals. The group uses advanced malware like FakeM, Psylo, and MobileOrder, expanding its attacks from PCs to mobile devices, and employing spear-phishing and watering hole tactics. This report aims to expose their methods to enhance awareness and improve countermeasures against this well-resourced adversary.

title: Internet Of Things (IoT) Predictions From Forrester, Machina Research, WEF, Gartner, IDC
summary: This article compiles predictions for the Internet of Things (IoT) from prominent research firms like Forrester, Machina Research, WEF, Gartner, and IDC. It highlights a shift from product sales to service provision, the growing importance of IoT security and analytics, and significant market growth and adoption across both consumer and enterprise sectors, despite some skepticism regarding current offerings. The article details specific forecasts for spending, connected devices, new applications, and challenges such as security breaches and market fragmentation for the period up to 2025.

title: Trend Lifts Auto-Parts Demand; AutoZone, O'Reilly Near Highs
summary: The demand for auto parts is rising due to several market trends including low gasoline prices encouraging more driving, and the increasing average age of cars leading to more repairs. AutoZone's stock is performing well despite recent market pullbacks, benefiting from these trends that are boosting auto-parts retailers.

title: Archive for January, 2016
summary: This January 2016 archive from Crossing Wall Street outlines several financial market updates, including individual stock performances and earnings reports from companies like Balchem Corp., Stryker, Biogen, Ford Motor, Alliance Data Systems, Microsoft, and CR Bard. The articles also discuss macroeconomic views such as the Federal Reserve’s monetary policy and the impact of the strong dollar and oil prices on corporate earnings. Key events covered include the final Chicago College All-Star Game, the best-performing stock of the last 30 years, and predictions for upcoming earnings reports.

title: Robert F. Smith (1962- )
summary: Robert F. Smith is celebrated as the founder, chairman, and CEO of Vista Equity Partners, a multi-billion-dollar private equity firm focusing on enterprise software. Ranked among the richest individuals in the U.S., Smith is also a significant philanthropist, known for major donations to educational institutions and initiatives supporting inner-city youth and African American advancement in technology and education. His career transitioned from engineering and patents to finance at Goldman Sachs before establishing his highly successful private equity venture.

title: Editas Medicine raises $94.4 million in year’s first IPO
summary: Editas Medicine Inc. became the first company to go public in the US this year, raising $94.4 million in an IPO by pricing shares at $16 each, at the low end of expectations. This IPO signals that going public remains an option for some biotech companies, despite volatile financial markets and a drop in the S&P 500 Index. Editas, a pioneer in gene editing, faces significant risks including a patent suit and potential regulatory restrictions, but its breakthrough technology has generated considerable interest.

title: Cisco to pay $1.4 billion for IoT firm Jasper
summary: Cisco Systems Inc. announced its acquisition of Jasper Technologies Inc., an Internet of Things (IoT) startup that connects various devices to the internet, for $1.4 billion in cash and equity. This move marks Cisco's largest acquisition since 2013 and is part of its strategy to find new growth avenues in the emerging IoT market, offering cutting-edge technology to its customers. Jasper's software platform helps monitor connected devices, a key aspect of Cisco's focus on the IoT space.

title: Apple, Inc set to open new $25 million tech center in Hyderabad, India by June
summary: Apple is reportedly opening its first technology development center in India, an investment of $25 million in Hyderabad, creating 4,500 jobs. This move signifies Apple's increased focus on the Indian market, following growing sales and efforts to open Apple Stores in the country. The article also details Apple's existing international facilities and R&D centers worldwide, highlighting its global expansion strategy.

title: 'Just John'
summary: John W. Thompson, chairman of Microsoft Corporation and CEO of Virtual Instruments, visited Florida A&M University (FAMU) to speak with students about his life and career. He shared his journey from a partying student to a successful businessman, emphasizing the importance of focus and execution over chasing a legacy. Thompson's visit also included meeting scholarship recipients funded by a $5 million donation from him and his wife.

title: Equinix Says Cloud Will Help It Reach Customers It Hasn't Reached Before
summary: Equinix expects cloud expansion to help it attract a significant number of new enterprise customers beyond its traditional core verticals. The company is positioning its data centers as hubs for private access to public clouds, aiming to expand its addressable market. This strategy has already led to increased customer acquisition, particularly in manufacturing and professional services.

title: Will Microsoft Corporation Launch A Lego-Like Surface Desktop?
summary: A published patent suggests Microsoft is considering a "modular" PC resembling Lego blocks, allowing for easy component swaps, potentially as a Surface device. While other companies have explored similar modular designs with limited success, Microsoft might aim to revolutionize the desktop market, especially for enterprise customers. However, the article argues that a modular PC would likely fail due to proprietary component costs, lack of industry standards, and the increasing irrelevance of individual component upgrades in modern computing.

title: Nanotechnology Company Exicure Raises Over $42 Million from Bill Gates, AbbVie, Agilent and Others
summary: Exicure, a nanotechnology company formerly known as AuraSense Therapeutics, has raised over $40.75 million in equity funding, including investments from prominent figures like Bill Gates and companies like AbbVie and Agilent. The company specializes in developing three-dimensional, spherical nucleic acid (SNA) architecture for immunomodulatory and gene silencing drugs, with a lead product, AST-005, targeting psoriasis. Exicure is preparing for a first-in-human Phase I trial in Germany and holds numerous patents for its SNA technology.

title: How Amazon became a dominant player in cloud services
summary: This article details Amazon Web Services' (AWS) rise to dominance in cloud computing, tracing its origins from an internal solution to a multi-billion dollar business. It highlights how AWS's customer-centric approach, low costs, and massive scale allowed it to outpace rivals and attract a wide range of clients from start-ups to government agencies. The piece also touches on Amazon's secretive operational culture and the intense work environment, while emphasizing AWS's critical role in technological advancements like powering Netflix and NASA's Mars Rover mission.

title: Autodesk part of software group backing Apple
summary: Autodesk is joining a consortium, including the Business Software Alliance, to file an amicus brief supporting Apple in its standoff with the FBI over iPhone access. Apple, and its supporters, contend that the FBI's request for new software could compromise user data and privacy, especially for international clients. While supporting data privacy, Autodesk's CEO Carl Bass also believes the FBI should get the information it needs in this specific case without setting a precedent for unfettered data access, suggesting a resolution behind closed doors.

title: Health Catalyst Raises $70 Million Led By Norwest Venture Partners and UPMC
summary: Health Catalyst announced a $70 million Series E funding round, co-led by Norwest Venture Partners and UPMC. The capital infusion, which also included contributions from existing customers MultiCare Health System and OSF Healthcare, as well as new and existing investors, will be used to expand Health Catalyst's product offerings in population health management, care management, cost accounting, and real-time decision support. The company reported significant growth in 2015 and anticipates becoming cash-flow sustainable by Q4 2016, making this likely its last private funding round.

title: Forbes Billionaires List Ranks Canadian David Thomson (And Family) At Number 25
summary: The Forbes Billionaires List for 2016 features several Canadians, with David Thomson and his family, primarily known for Thomson Reuters, ranking 25th globally with a net worth of $23.8 billion. Galen Weston and family also made the list in 116th place. Conversely, Michael Pearson of Valeant Pharmaceuticals saw a significant drop in his net worth and fell off the list due to company investigations.

title: Golisano, Pegula on Forbes' billionaire list
summary: Former Rochester-area businessman Tom Golisano and Buffalo Bills and Sabres owner Terry Pegula have once again been named to Forbes' list of the world's richest people. Golisano, founder of Paychex Inc., is listed at No. 688 with a net worth of $2.5 billion, while Pegula is ranked No. 380 with an estimated worth of $4 billion. Meanwhile, J. Michael Pearson, CEO of Valeant Pharmaceuticals International, fell out of the rankings due to a significant loss in company value.

title: This Storage Company Just Initiated Layoffs
summary: NetApp has begun its previously announced layoffs, impacting approximately 1,500 employees or 12% of its workforce. CEO George Kurian stated these cuts are a difficult but necessary step for the company's transformation, aiming for greater focus and efficiency. The restructuring comes two months after acquiring Solidfire for $870 million and amidst challenges from public cloud storage providers.

title: International Business Machines Corp. (NYSE:IBM) Consistently Returns Money to Shareholders
summary: Peter Siphron of Siphron Capital Management highlights International Business Machines Corp. (NYSE:IBM) as a company that consistently generates profits and returns money to shareholders through share buybacks. Despite a "bumpy" transition from legacy hardware to software and services, IBM leverages its Watson AI and cloud services for future growth, competing with major players in the cloud sector. Siphron emphasizes IBM's ability to extract consistent profit from modest sales growth.

title: Zillow's growth, scope surprises even its leaders
summary: Rich Barton, co-founder of Zillow and Expedia, and Zillow Group CEO Spencer Rascoff discuss the rapid growth and unexpected influence of Zillow. The company, which recently celebrated its 10th anniversary, has expanded significantly, becoming a major player in the real estate industry and forging partnerships with 13,000 brokers and 400 MLSs. They also touch on Zillow's workplace culture, its origin stemming from the desire to empower consumers with information, and future technological advancements like VR and streamlined transaction processes.

title: Apple Using Google’s Cloud, Moving Some Data From Amazon
summary: Apple Inc. is reportedly moving some of its data from Amazon.com Inc.'s cloud services to Google's computing-on-demand service. This move represents a significant win for Alphabet Inc.'s Google in its competition with Amazon and Microsoft Corp. for cloud computing customers. It also signals Google's progress in the growing $26 billion cloud computing market.

title: Dominion, Microsoft partner on 20 MW solar farm in Virginia
summary: Dominion is partnering with Microsoft and the state of Virginia to develop a 20 MW solar project in Fauquier County. This initiative is part of Dominion's commitment to building 400 MW of solar energy in Virginia by 2020. Microsoft will purchase and retire the green credits to support its sustainability goals, and the project is slated for service in late 2017 subject to regulatory approval.

title: Mercury lands Google veteran Ryan Brack for tech and innovation group
summary: Mercury has hired Ryan Brack, a Google veteran and former aide to the NYC Mayor's office, as an SVP to bolster its technology and innovation team, based in New York. This move, along with the launch of a San Francisco office last fall, significantly enhances the Omnicom firm's capacity to provide expert technology counsel to clients. Brack aims to penetrate the European market and replicate tech industry innovation in New York, while Mercury continues to serve a diverse client roster including eBay, Microsoft, Pfizer, and Uber.

title: Hewlett Packard Enterprise and Microsoft Just Invested Millions In This Hot Startup
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) and Microsoft (MSFT) co-led a $73.5 million funding round for data center software startup Mesosphere, bringing its total funding to $126 million. Mesosphere's technology helps optimize data center resources for software applications, and the company sells commercial packages combining its open-source Mesos technology with proprietary software. The investment highlights competition in the data center efficiency market, with companies like Google, Amazon, and Docker offering similar solutions.

title: Evolution of SamSa Malware Suggests New Ransomware Tactics In Play
summary: This article details the evolution of the SamSa ransomware, first observed in December 2015, highlighting a shift towards targeted attacks rather than broad-net phishing campaigns. It discusses how the malware is manually deployed post-compromise using common system administrator tools and outlines its technical changes over time, including code obfuscation, file extension variations, ransom notice alterations, and changes in Bitcoin demands. Palo Alto Networks also tracks the attacker's profits and speculates on possible links to high-profile ransomware incidents.

title: Google CEO Sundar Pichai was paid over $100 MILLION on his first year in the job
summary: Google CEO Sundar Pichai received over $100 million in compensation during his first year, according to a recent public filing. This included a $652,500 annual salary and $99.8 million in restricted stock in 2015, with an additional $199 million in restricted shares awarded last month. The significant compensation comes as Google's parent company, Alphabet, surpassed Apple to become the world's most valuable public company.

title: Sphere 3D Introduces SnapSync(TM), Enterprise-Class File Synchronization and Share Solution
summary: Sphere 3D Corp. announced SnapSync™, an enterprise-class file synchronization and share solution designed for private and hybrid cloud deployments. This highly secure software offers centralized IT control, immediate disaster recovery, and compatibility across various devices and operating systems, addressing concerns about data security and management in enterprise environments. SnapSync aims to provide a cost-effective, secure, and scalable solution for businesses, leveraging Sphere 3D's existing Snap storage infrastructure and targeting new vertical markets such as education.

title: Amazon to open Hyderabad campus by 2019
summary: Amazon.com Inc. is set to open its largest campus outside the US in Hyderabad by 2019, a significant investment in one of its fastest-growing markets. The 3-million-square-foot facility will house thousands of employees managing back-end operations and a technology development center. This move underscores Amazon's long-term commitment and investment in India, positioning it alongside other major tech companies like Apple, Microsoft, and Google which are also expanding their presence in Hyderabad.

title: Apple turns 40 today. It almost didn’t make it to 20
summary: On Apple's 40th birthday, this article revisits a 1996 report when the company was struggling, with its stock price around $1 per share and significant layoffs. The piece contrasts Apple's proprietary system with Microsoft's open approach, which initially led to Apple's difficulties, but highlights how changes like opening its OS and the rise of the internet, along with Steve Jobs's return, revitalized the company, making it incredibly successful today. It also notes the ironic shift where Apple now benefits from user "path dependency" similar to what Microsoft once enjoyed.

title: NVIDIA Launches World's First Deep Learning Supercomputer
summary: NVIDIA has unveiled the NVIDIA DGX-1, which it claims is the world's first deep learning supercomputer designed to meet the demands of artificial intelligence. This system integrates hardware, deep learning software, and development tools, delivering the equivalent throughput of 250 x86 servers. Powered by NVIDIA Tesla P100 GPUs and built on the new NVIDIA Pascal GPU architecture, the DGX-1 aims to significantly accelerate the training of sophisticated deep neural networks.

title: Tesla poached a team of chip architects and execs from AMD to develop the next gen Autopilot
summary: Tesla has significantly expanded its Autopilot team by hiring top chip architects and executives from AMD, following the earlier recruitment of legendary chip architect Jim Keller. This move suggests Tesla is developing its second-generation Autopilot hardware to enable fully autonomous driving, potentially hinting at the company designing its own chips despite past collaborations with NVIDIA and Mobileye. The new hires include key figures like David Glasco, Thaddeus Fortenberry, Debjit Das Sarma, and Keith Witek, all working under Keller's leadership.

title: Report: Amazon acquires AI photo tech startup Orbeus
summary: Amazon.com Inc. reportedly acquired AI-powered photo recognition startup Orbeus Inc. in late 2015, a move that aligns with other tech giants acquiring AI companies. The acquisition is seen as a strategic investment to boost Amazon Web Services (AWS) and automate warehouse operations, particularly given rising fulfillment costs and AWS's critical role in Amazon's financial performance.

title: Rackspace Offers Customers ‘Cloud in a Box’
summary: Rackspace is launching a new "cloud in a box" offering that provides servers, storage, and networking gear in an enclosure, ships it to a customer's chosen data center, and manages it for a fee. This service uses OpenStack, an open-source cloud framework, and aims to cater to existing Rackspace customers with geographical deployment needs or companies tired of managing their own IT. Rackspace is extending its support, previously for its own cloud products, to include AWS and Azure, with future plans to support other platforms like VMware and MongoDB.

title: Turtle Beach Impact 500 Mechanical Keyboard Review
summary: The Turtle Beach Impact 500 mechanical keyboard is reviewed as a simple, compact, and solid option for TKL fans looking for a no-frills experience. While it works with Macs and older PCs and has little extraneous key noise, its price is considered a bit steep for a basic model, especially given the use of Costar stabilizers. The article delves into its design, specifications, and performance, noting Turtle Beach's entry into the gaming peripherals market.

title: The Two Women Who Kicked Off Salesforce's Company-Wide Salary Review
summary: Leyla Seka and Cindy Robbins, two senior Salesforce employees, successfully convinced CEO Marc Benioff to conduct an internal salary audit that revealed and corrected gender-pay disparities, costing the company $3 million. Their initiative, born from their involvement in the Women’s Surge program, led to 6% of employees receiving raises for equal pay. Seka and Robbins hope their experience encourages other companies to address pay equality, emphasizing the importance of transparency and courage.

title: Microsoft and Soloinsight to Help Build Internet of "People" Together
summary: Microsoft has chosen Soloinsight for its Azure IoT Red Carpet program to jointly develop the Internet of "People" based on the Azure IoT infrastructure. Soloinsight's CloudGate platform, an access intelligence software, will leverage Azure IoT to make conventional gates and turnstiles smart, aiming to identify people flawlessly, enforce compliance, aggregate data, and allow seamless physical single sign-on access. This collaboration targets the burgeoning IoT market, with an estimated $6 trillion to be spent on IoT solutions in the next five years.

title: President Obama appoints Microsoft Research VP Peter Lee as a member of a cybersecurity commission
summary: President Barack Obama has appointed Peter Lee, Corporate Vice President of Microsoft Research, to the Commission on Enhancing National Cybersecurity. Lee joined Microsoft in 2010 and previously served at the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency and Carnegie Mellon University. The commission's goal is to identify steps to ensure national cybersecurity in an increasingly digital world.

title: Silicon Valley Mourns Loss of ‘Coach’ Bill Campbell
summary: Silicon Valley is mourning the death of Bill Campbell, a renowned mentor and former football coach, who passed away after a long battle with cancer. Campbell was celebrated for his ability to coach and counsel top tech executives at companies like Apple, Google, and Intuit, and for his quiet advocacy for women in technology. Many prominent figures in the tech industry, including Tim Cook and Eric Schmidt, shared their condolences and memories of Campbell on social media, highlighting his significant impact on their careers and the industry.

title: Gartner’s 2016 Endpoint Protection Magic Quadrant: What’s Changed?
summary: This article reviews Gartner's 2016 Endpoint Protection Platforms Magic Quadrant, detailing changes in vendor positioning since 2014. It highlights movements within the Niche Players, Visionaries, Challengers, and Leaders quadrants, attributing these shifts to factors like company mergers, product development, and evolving market trends such as cloud options and ransomware protection. The report emphasizes how different vendors are adapting to the changing landscape of endpoint security.

title: Real Accounting Numbers Paint Dark Picture Of Blackbaud
summary: This article argues that Blackbaud (BLKB) is a stock to avoid due to misleading non-GAAP metrics, declining economic earnings, and inefficient management of capital. Despite impressive revenue growth, the company's true cash flows have declined, and its profitability is threatened by competition and an unprofitable niche market. The article concludes that BLKB is significantly overvalued, even considering potential acquisition scenarios or organic growth projections.

title: AMD Stock Up 52%, The Highest Climb Since Its Listing
summary: AMD's stock surged 52% to $3.99, marking its highest single-day gain since its 1979 listing, driven by a strong Q1 2016 report and optimistic Q2 outlook. The company announced a lucrative joint venture for x86 chips in China and revealed three new semicustom wins estimated at $1.5 billion, with anticipated product launches like Polaris GPUs and Zen CPUs expected to significantly boost future earnings. These new products are crucial for AMD's long-term success and market re-entry into high-end CPU segments.

title: Hey, Nokia Isn't Just a Company That Used to Make Phones
summary: This article discusses Nokia's evolution beyond its former mobile phone business, highlighting its successful transition into selling high-end networking gear and software. It examines Nokia's recent acquisition of Withings, a company specializing in smart home and wearable products, and contextualizes this move within Nokia's long history as a diversified holding company making strategic investments in emerging markets. The piece suggests that Nokia's ventures into consumer electronics and health technologies, like the Withings acquisition and the OZO VR camera, are akin to Alphabet's "other bets," positioning Nokia to capitalize on future big trends.

title: Sharing insights elevates their impact
summary: ExxonMobil lost its coveted AAA credit rating despite beating earnings expectations, with S&P downgrading it to AA due to future debt headwinds from low oil prices. Meanwhile, investors are flocking to emerging market bonds, as evidenced by significant inflows into ETFs and the strong performance of the iShares Emerging Markets Local Government Bond ETF. The Bank of Japan's decision to hold interest rates, rather than further negative rates, was welcomed by Japanese bank credit.

title: Facebook’s Oculus Rift Virtual Reality Headset Is Coming to Best Buy
summary: Facebook's Oculus Rift virtual reality headset will soon be available for demo and purchase at 48 Best Buy locations across the United States starting May 7th, with more stores to follow. This initiative aims to allow consumers to experience the VR headset firsthand, as Oculus works to fulfill existing pre-orders. Additionally, a limited number of Rifts will be sold online via Microsoft and Amazon.

title: HP announces redesigned portfolio of Windows 10 PCs
summary: HP Inc. unveiled a redesigned portfolio of Windows 10 PCs, including convertibles, notebooks, and desktops, aimed at students and families. These new devices feature updated color options, B&O PLAY audio, 6th generation Intel processors, and Windows Hello biometric authentication. The article details the specific features, pricing, and availability of the HP Pavilion x360, HP Pavilion All-in-Ones, and HP Pavilion Desktop.

title: Google Chrome Edges Internet Explorer As Most Popular Web Browser
summary: Google Chrome has surpassed Microsoft's Internet Explorer to become the most popular web browser globally, according to NetMarketShare.com data for April. Chrome controlled 41.66% of the market, while IE and Microsoft Edge collectively held 41.35%. This marks a significant shift, largely driven by Microsoft's decision to discontinue IE development in favor of Edge, benefiting Chrome's market share.

title: Virtual Field Trip: An Inside Look at Corning’s Sullivan Park Research & Development Campus #LearningThroughGorillaGlass
summary: This article provides an inside look at Corning's Sullivan Park Research & Development Campus, highlighting their long history in glass innovation beyond PYREX and CorningWare. It details how Corning scientists developed Gorilla Glass 4 by understanding glass breakage and replicating real-world drop scenarios through rigorous testing, and touches on the ion-exchange chemical strengthening process. The article also announces a contest for a mother-daughter pair to visit Corning's facilities and meet their female scientists.

title: 60 seconds with Hugh Milward
summary: Hugh Milward, newly appointed Senior Director of Corporate, External and Legal Affairs at Microsoft UK, discusses his role, aims, and challenges. He brings a non-legal background to focus on "outside-in" policy, emphasizing listening to societal views and empowering individuals through technology. Milward highlights the importance of privacy and security in the evolving tech landscape and his passion for fairness.

title: Microsoft Corporation to Stop Nagging Users to Update to Windows 10
summary: Microsoft announced it will cease "nagging" Windows 7 and Windows 8 users to upgrade to Windows 10 starting July 29, 2016. This date marks the end of the free upgrade offer, after which users will need to purchase the operating system. The company will also begin removing the upgrade app from user devices.

title: Hands-on with Garmin’s new Vivosmart HR+ (now with GPS)
summary: This article provides a hands-on review of Garmin's new Vivosmart HR+ activity tracker, highlighting its key new features like built-in GPS, running workout modes, and Move IQ, distinguishing it from its predecessor, the Vivosmart HR. It also offers a market comparison with other devices like the Microsoft Band 2, Fitbit Blaze, and Garmin Vivoactive HR, noting its strengths and weaknesses. The author praises its technical capabilities while acknowledging potential trade-offs in battery life and accuracy due to the compact GPS integration.

title: ServiceNow Cloud Management adds Microsoft Azure support
summary: ServiceNow's Cloud Management suite now supports Microsoft Azure infrastructure, expanding its capabilities beyond Amazon Web Services and VMware. This integration offers a unified system for automating cloud management, providing templates for self-service requests, a single security model, and tools for managing total cost of ownership and compliance. The company plans to add support for more public cloud providers in the future.

title: NVIDIA GRID Delivers 100 Graphics-Accelerated Virtual Desktops per Server
summary: NVIDIA introduced NVIDIA GRID with the new NVIDIA Tesla M10 GPU, enabling up to 128 graphics-accelerated virtual desktops per server. This offering aims to make virtualizing enterprise applications more affordable and accessible for all employees, enhancing user experience for a wide range of business applications, including those that are GPU-accelerated. The Tesla M10 joins other Tesla GPUs as part of a flexible solution for various enterprise user needs.

title: Nokia returns to the phone market as Microsoft sells brand
summary: Microsoft has sold the Nokia brand name, which it had previously acquired, in two parts for $350m, enabling Nokia to re-enter the mobile phone market. A new Finnish company, HMD, formed by ex-Nokia employees, acquired the brand, while iPhone manufacturer Foxconn bought the manufacturing and distribution arms and will build new Nokia phones. The new entity plans to develop Nokia-branded smartphones and tablets running Android, appealing to consumers nostalgic for the brand.

title: Microsoft to sell feature phone business to Foxconn subsidiary, HMD Global
summary: Microsoft announced it is selling its entry-level feature phone business, including brands, software, and services, to FIH Mobile Ltd (a Foxconn subsidiary) and HMD Global Oy for $350 million. As part of the deal, FIH Mobile will also acquire Microsoft Mobile Vietnam, and approximately 4,500 employees will transfer to the new companies. Microsoft plans to continue developing Windows 10 Mobile and supporting Lumia phones from OEM partners.

title: Minecraft is headed to China
summary: Microsoft and Mojang have partnered with NetEase, Inc. to bring a tailored version of Minecraft to the Chinese market. This strategic move aims to expand Minecraft's global community and introduce the game to a vast new player base in China.

title: Microsoft And Mojang Partner With NetEase To Launch Minecraft In China
summary: Microsoft, Mojang, and NetEase have announced a partnership to bring Minecraft to the Chinese market. This exclusive five-year agreement will see Mojang develop a version of Minecraft tailored for China, to be released in partnership with NetEase. Both companies expressed excitement about expanding Minecraft's reach to China's large user base.

title: 'Minecraft' is making its way to China
summary: Mojang is partnering with Chinese internet company NetEase to bring a special edition of Minecraft to China. This version will be tailored for Chinese gamers and will initially launch for PC and mobile devices. NetEase CEO, William Ding, expressed excitement about introducing the game to China's vast user base.

title: Ingram Micro Adds Dropbox to Cloud Marketplace in Singapore
summary: Ingram Micro announced the addition of Dropbox Business to its Cloud Marketplace in Singapore, responding to increased demand for secure, cloud-based file sharing services in Asia Pacific. This integration allows channel partners to seamlessly purchase, provision, configure, and manage Dropbox Business through a single automated platform, enhancing collaboration capabilities and opening new business opportunities. The move aims to boost cloud profitability for channel partners by offering an affordable, secure, and easily bundled solution with other offerings like Microsoft Office 365, targeting the largely untapped SMB market.

title: Cyber Security Report 2025
summary: This page is dedicated to Check Point Software's "Cyber Security Report 2025." It serves as a central hub for downloading the full report and provides an overview of various Check Point products, solutions, and services related to cybersecurity. The content emphasizes Check Point's comprehensive offerings for different industries and business sizes.

title: Wingstop debuts social ordering platform
summary: Wingstop has launched a new social ordering platform on Twitter and Facebook Messenger, allowing customers to place and customize orders directly through these channels by sending the word "order" to the brand. This initiative aims to engage with customers where they already are, particularly Millennials, and bypasses the need for app downloads or profile creation. The platform is being rolled out to 815 domestic locations and future phases will include proactive outreach to customers based on their indicated interest.

title: Salesforce to open centre in Hyderabad
summary: Salesforce.com Inc. is expanding its operations in India by opening a centre of excellence in Hyderabad, creating 1,000 jobs. This will make Hyderabad its biggest hub in India and one of its largest engineering and customer service centres globally, also serving as the headquarters for its India operations. Salesforce's decision mirrors similar moves by other tech giants like Google, Amazon, and Uber to establish significant presences in the city.

title: Enfish, LLC v. Microsoft Corporation : A Victory For Software Patents
summary: The article discusses the Enfish, LLC v. Microsoft Corporation case, where the U.S. Federal Circuit reversed a district court's decision invalidating two software patents. The court found Enfish's patents eligible as they improved computer functionality, providing clarity on the Alice test and expanding patent-eligible subject matter for software. This decision offers hope for software patentees and is expected to influence future patent eligibility evaluations.

title: Precision Gaming Mice - Introduction
summary: This article introduces a round-up review of three precision gaming mice: the Tesoro Sagitta Spectrum H6L, Corsair M65 Pro RGB, and Logitech G900 Chaos Spectrum. It discusses the importance of choosing the right mouse, different grip styles (palm, claw, fingertip), and how these mice were tested across various surfaces and gaming genres (MOBA, RTS, FPS).

title: AECOM and Trimble Pioneering Use of Mixed-Reality Technology for Engineering and Construction
summary: AECOM and Trimble are collaborating on the world's first use of Microsoft HoloLens "mixed-reality" technology for engineering and construction, launching a pilot program on three continents. This technology, which uses a lightweight headset to add holograms of 3D objects into a user's view, aims to improve communication, collaboration, and visualization in complex projects. The initiative is already being applied to real-world projects like the Serpentine Galleries' annual architecture program in London, demonstrating its potential to accelerate the engineering design process and enable simultaneous exploration of holographic projections by remote teams.

title: Microsoft to acquire LinkedIn - Source
summary: Microsoft Corporation announced its definitive agreement to acquire LinkedIn Corporation for $196 per share in an all-cash transaction valued at $26.2 billion. LinkedIn will maintain its distinct brand and independence, with Jeff Weiner remaining CEO and reporting to Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella. The acquisition, expected to close in 2016, aims to accelerate the growth of both companies by combining Microsoft's cloud services with LinkedIn's professional network.

title: Microsoft to Acquire LinkedIn at a Premium
summary: Microsoft announced its acquisition of professional networking platform LinkedIn for $26.2 billion in an all-cash deal, paying a 50 percent premium over LinkedIn's recent share price. This acquisition aims to combine Microsoft's professional cloud with LinkedIn's professional network, with LinkedIn maintaining its brand and current CEO Jeff Weiner. The deal comes after LinkedIn's shares had fallen significantly due to a cautious financial outlook.

title: Microsoft to acquire LinkedIn
summary: Microsoft announced its definitive agreement to acquire LinkedIn for $196 per share in an all-cash transaction valued at $26.2 billion. LinkedIn will maintain its distinct brand, culture, and independence, with Jeff Weiner remaining CEO and reporting to Satya Nadella. title: LinkedIn’s deal gives Empire State Building a new luster
summary: Microsoft's acquisition of LinkedIn is expected to further boost the "cool factor" of the Empire State Building, where LinkedIn has expanded significantly since 2013. The article details the skyscraper's transformation from a "Class B-minus" office location to a prestigious commercial hub, attributing its revival to major capital improvements and strategic tenant acquisitions by Empire State Realty Trust. This revitalization has attracted high-profile tenants like LinkedIn, Shutterstock, Coty, and Bulova, drastically improving the building's commercial profile and leasing performance.

title: Why Microsoft Likes LinkedIn (Published 2016)
summary: Microsoft acquired LinkedIn for $26.2 billion, the largest acquisition in its history, aiming to enhance its relevance in the cloud computing and corporate software markets. Despite LinkedIn incurring losses on its revenue, Microsoft sees potential synergy by integrating it into its existing human resources and financial planning products. The acquisition positions Microsoft to compete for the global market in corporate computing and leverage LinkedIn's vast user data.

title: Does Microsoft’s $26.2 Billion Splurge On LinkedIn Make Sense? A Tear Down Analysis !
summary: Microsoft's acquisition of LinkedIn for $26.2 billion is analyzed to understand its strategic rationale. The article explores how this acquisition addresses Microsoft's need for new revenue streams beyond declining PC sales, boosts its enterprise cloud solutions, and provides LinkedIn with growth opportunities and access to a larger market. Despite concerns about the high price tag, the author argues that the integration of both companies' strengths makes strategic sense for future growth.

title: What are the 5 biggest internet buyouts of all time?
summary: This article lists and describes the five largest internet buyouts in history, prompted by Microsoft's $26.2 billion acquisition of LinkedIn in 2016. It details each acquisition, including Microsoft's previous purchase of Skype, Oracle's acquisition of Peoplesoft, Facebook's buyout of WhatsApp, and the historic AOL-Time Warner merger. The article highlights the financial figures and the strategic context or outcome of each deal, including the Dot Com Bubble's impact on the AOL-Time Warner merger.

title: Microsoft to acquire LinkedIn for $26.2 billion in an all-cash deal
summary: Microsoft Corp. announced an agreement to acquire LinkedIn for $26.2 billion in an all-cash deal, with LinkedIn retaining its brand and independence. Jeff Weiner will remain CEO of LinkedIn, reporting to Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella. The transaction, expected to close in 2016, aims to accelerate the growth of LinkedIn, Microsoft Office 365, and Dynamics.

title: The First Big Company to Say It’s Serving the Legal Marijuana Trade? Microsoft. (Published 2016)
summary: Microsoft is breaking industry taboos by partnering to offer “seed to sale” tracking software for the legal marijuana trade, becoming the first major corporation to openly serve this market. This move into government compliance for cannabis suggests the beginning of a legitimate infrastructure for a rapidly growing industry, despite federal illegality. Microsoft anticipates significant growth and increasingly sophisticated requirements in a regulated marijuana market.

title: Microsoft Is Fighting a New Rule on How Corporations Must Treat Contract Workers
summary: Microsoft is challenging a 2015 National Labor Relations Board ruling that expanded the definition of a "joint employer," arguing it could have significant negative implications for the technology company and discourage corporate social responsibility initiatives. The ruling broadened the criteria for joint employment, potentially making companies more responsible for contract workers, which Microsoft fears will deter them from requiring contractors to provide employee benefits. The company, alongside other business groups, claims the decision is too broad and could disrupt various business-to-business relationships.

title: Ellison Has Some Fighting Words for Frenemy Salesforce
summary: Oracle's Executive Chairman Larry Ellison has made a bold claim that Oracle will be the first company to reach $10 billion in annual software-as-a-service and platform-as-a-service sales, directly challenging rival Salesforce, which currently dominates the SaaS market. This move highlights Oracle's aggressive push into cloud computing, seeking to rapidly catch up with competitors like Salesforce, Amazon, Microsoft, and IBM. The article details the ongoing rivalry between Oracle and Salesforce CEOs and Oracle's strategy to achieve this revenue milestone by leveraging its broader software categories.

title: Sari-sari stores with WiFi in PH soon, to be funded by Microsoft
summary: A Quezon City-based startup, WiFi Interactive Network (WIN), secured US$150,000 in seed funding from Microsoft's Affordable Access Initiative. The funding will support WIN's plan to install 10,000 WiFi hotspots in the Philippines, starting in July, by transforming sari-sari stores into connectivity hubs using TV White Space (TVWS) technology. This initiative aims to improve internet access across the country, especially in areas outside Metro Manila.

title: Coupa Software Positioned as Leader in Gartner 2016 Magic Quadrant for Procure-to-Pay Suites
summary: Coupa Software has been recognized as a Leader in Gartner's 2016 Magic Quadrant for Procure-to-Pay Suites for the second consecutive year, achieving the highest 'ability to execute' assessment. The company's CEO, Rob Bernshteyn, highlighted their commitment to customer success and measurable value creation. Coupa continues to expand its platform and network, connecting 2 million suppliers and enabling significant customer savings.

title: Why is Microsoft keeping two Vancouver offices?
summary: Microsoft maintains two offices in Vancouver due to the need for secrecy in game development, specifically for Gears of War 4. The new Microsoft Canada Excellence Centre at Pacific Centre accommodates 388 employees with capacity for 750, focusing on projects like OneNote, interactive TV, Skype, and HoloLens, while 180 video-game developers remain at the Pivotal Building for classified work. Future work is also anticipated following Microsoft's acquisition of LinkedIn.

title: Prince of Persia – Game Over
summary: Unit 42 successfully gained control of multiple C2 domains used in a decade-long "Prince of Persia" malware campaign, effectively disabling the attackers' access to most victims. This article details the sinkhole operation, victim analysis, malware version breakdown, and recent attacker activities observed after the initial publication. The campaign ended after cooperation with law enforcement to null-route remaining C2 domains and disable the directly IP-addressed server.

title: Adobe Is the Leader in Gartner’s Magic Quadrant, Again
summary: Adobe announced its recognition by Gartner as a leader in the 2016 Magic Quadrant for Mobile App Development Platforms, marking its fourth consecutive year in this position. Despite this achievement, Adobe lags behind IBM and Salesforce.com in execution and Microsoft in vision within the mobile app development space. The company also introduced new features in Creative Cloud and aims to boost its Marketing Cloud and mobile app development presence through the LiveFyre acquisition.

title: Microsoft could overtake Amazon in the cloud, Morgan Stanley survey finds
summary: A Morgan Stanley survey of CIOs indicates that Microsoft Azure could surpass Amazon Web Services (AWS) in future cloud adoption, despite AWS currently holding a larger market share. While more CIOs use AWS now, projections suggest a slight majority plan to use Azure within three years, largely due to Microsoft's existing enterprise product integration. The survey also highlights increasing public cloud adoption and identifies cloud, business intelligence/analytics, and security as top IT spending priorities, even as overall IT budget growth slows.

title: Ch-ch-ch-changes at Microsoft as COO Kevin Turner heads for the exits
summary: Microsoft COO Kevin Turner is leaving the company after 11 years to become CEO of Citadel Securities. CEO Satya Nadella announced that Turner's responsibilities would be distributed among five people, signaling a continued shift in leadership and strategy at Microsoft. This departure follows other executive exits and further consolidates Nadella's influence over the company's direction.

title: Fast-growing Alibaba Cloud promotes ex-Microsoft exec Jingren Zhou to chief scientist
summary: Alibaba Cloud, the cloud computing arm of Alibaba Group, has appointed former Microsoft executive Jingren Zhou as its chief scientist to lead big-data and artificial intelligence research. Zhou will manage a team in China and the U.S. focused on developing technology in speech, natural language, image/video processing, and large-scale machine learning. Alibaba Cloud, a fast-growing business within the Alibaba Group, saw its revenue triple in its fourth fiscal quarter to over 1 billion yuan (US$149.6 million).

title: Apple, Microsoft, HP among companies shunning GOP convention
summary: Several major corporations, including Apple, Microsoft, and HP Inc., are withholding financial and product support from the 2016 Republican National Convention, a departure from their past donations. While companies cite various reasons, their decisions are widely seen as a response to Donald Trump's controversial rhetoric. Many of these companies are also not supporting the Democratic convention, but their withdrawal from the GOP event is more significant given their past support.

title: GE and Microsoft partner to bring Predix to Azure, accelerating digital transformation for industrial customers
summary: GE and Microsoft announced a strategic partnership to bring GE's Predix platform for the Industrial Internet to Microsoft Azure, aiming to accelerate digital transformation for industrial customers. This collaboration will allow businesses to capture intelligence from industrial assets and leverage Microsoft's enterprise cloud applications, integrating Predix with Azure IoT Suite, Cortana Intelligence Suite, and Microsoft business applications. A developer preview is expected by late 2016, with commercial availability by Q2 2017.

title: Malware Discovered – SFG: Furtim Malware Analysis
summary: SentinelOne Labs discovered a sophisticated malware campaign, SFG: Furtim, targeting an energy company, which exhibits traits of a nation-state sponsored initiative, likely from Eastern Europe. The malware employs extreme measures to evade detection by bypassing traditional antivirus, next-gen firewalls, and sandboxing techniques, affecting all versions of Microsoft Windows. It utilizes various anti-analysis techniques, local privilege escalation exploits, and aims to remove antivirus software before deploying its final payload to collect reconnaissance.

title: Microsoft appoints Corporate Vice-President for Europe Middle-East Africa
summary: Microsoft has appointed Michel van der Bel as the new Corporate Vice-President of Europe, Middle-East and Africa. In this role, he will lead Microsoft’s business across 32 subsidiaries, encompassing 134 markets and nearly 20,000 employees, focusing on digital transformation and cloud-first, mobile-first strategies. Van der Bel, a 13-year Microsoft veteran, previously served as Area Vice President for Microsoft UK and chief operating officer for Microsoft in Greater China.

title: The Rebirth of Nokia: An Interview with Chairman Risto Siilasmaa
summary: This article features an interview with Nokia Chairman Risto Siilasmaa, discussing the company's dramatic transformation from near bankruptcy in 2012 to a renewed focus on networking and the "programmable world." Siilasmaa details the strategic decisions, including selling the phone and mapping businesses, and the internal changes that led to Nokia's enterprise value growing twenty-fold. He also shares key advice for leaders undergoing major transformations, emphasizing independent thinking, paranoid optimism, and building a strong team.

title: Scotts Miracle Gro to Invest $500M in Legal Cannabis by End of Year
summary: Scotts Miracle-Gro plans to invest $500 million in the legal cannabis production industry by the end of 2016 to counter flat sales and re-energize the company. CEO Jim Hagedorn identified the cannabis sector, particularly hydroponic supplies, as a significant growth opportunity, leading to acquisitions like General Hydroponics and a new product line, Black Magic. This move signals a larger trend of major companies, including Microsoft, entering the rapidly expanding legal marijuana market.

title: Sprinklr Raises Fund Value to $1.8 Billion to Help Enterprises Unify Their Front Office
summary: Sprinklr announced new funding of $105 million, valuing the company at $1.8 billion, bringing its total funding to $239 million. The round was led by Temasek, with participation from Wellington Management Company LLP and EDBI, alongside existing investors. This investment aims to help enterprises unify their front office operations, leveraging Sprinklr's social media management platform to enhance customer experience.

title: Is the sale of ARM a 'surrender' or an 'endorsement' for the UK?
summary: The article discusses the controversial £24bn acquisition of UK tech firm ARM Holdings by Japanese company Softbank. It explores arguments from critics who view it as a surrender of British innovation and warn of potential job losses and compromised independence, contrasting these with perspectives that see the investment as an endorsement of UK tech and a necessary step for ARM to compete globally. The deal’s impact on Softbank’s share price and potential rival bids are also examined.

title: Chinese consortium agrees $4.4 billion deal for Caesars online games
summary: A Chinese consortium, including Shanghai Giant Network Technology Co Ltd and Alibaba founder Jack Ma, has agreed to acquire Caesars Interactive Entertainment Inc's online games unit, Playtika, for $4.4 billion in cash. This deal will provide a significant boost to Caesars Acquisition Co and Caesars Entertainment Corp as they navigate a complex merger and a large bankruptcy restructuring. The acquisition highlights Chinese companies' growing interest in expanding their presence in the global online gaming market.

title: Microsoft to acquire LinkedIn for $26.2bn
summary: Microsoft Corporation announced its acquisition of LinkedIn Corporation for $26.2 billion in an all-cash transaction, marking Microsoft's largest acquisition to date. The deal, expected to close in 2016, will see LinkedIn retain its brand and independence, with CEO Jeff Weiner reporting directly to Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella. Microsoft anticipates the deal to be minimally dilutive to non-GAAP earnings per share in the short term, becoming accretive in fiscal year 2019.

title: Salesforce buys word processing app Quip for $750M
summary: Salesforce has acquired Quip, a cloud-based word processing app co-founded by Bret Taylor, for $750 million in cash and shares. This acquisition expands Salesforce's cloud-based app offerings beyond CRM and intensifies its competition with Microsoft in the enterprise market. Quip will continue to operate independently under Salesforce, with its co-founders remaining with the company.

title: Why This 160-Year-Old Company Is Embracing Cloud Apps
summary: Western Union, a 160-year-old money transfer company, is embracing cloud applications to modernize its operations. They have partnered with Box for document archiving and sharing among its 10,000 employees and contractors, valuing Box's deletion schedule control and governance features. Additionally, Western Union uses Conga, a Salesforce-affiliated firm, to automate government-required follow-up letters to customers, streamlining a previously manual process.

title: HP Spectre 13: A Month With What Could Be The Sexiest Laptop Alive
summary: Patrick Moorhead reviews the HP Spectre 13 after a month of use, highlighting its incredibly thin design, premium build quality, and surprisingly high-performance components for such a slim device. He discusses its features like the piston hinge, Intel Core i7 processor, PCIe storage, and USB Type-C ports with Thunderbolt 3, as well as the trade-offs such as the non-touch display and battery life under continuous use. Moorhead concludes that the Spectre 13 is a marvel of engineering, setting a new standard for premium, thin, and light laptops.

title: Apple Says It Has Fixed Gender Pay Gap For U.S. Employees
summary: Apple has announced that it has closed the gender wage gap for its employees in the United States, with women and underrepresented minorities earning one dollar for every dollar male and white employees earn, respectively. The company is now analyzing its global workforce to address any existing pay disparities worldwide. This achievement aligns with similar announcements from Facebook and Amazon and reflects Apple's focus on hiring more women and diverse candidates, with a slight shift in its workforce composition and over half of new hires being minorities.

title: Musical Chairs: Cadwalader Antitrust Stars Decamp For Paul, Weiss
summary: Four antitrust partners, including rainmaker Charles "Rick" Rule, are leaving Cadwalader, Wickersham & Taft to join Paul, Weiss Rifkind, Wharton & Garrison. This move is seen as a significant win for Paul, Weiss, which is on a lateral hiring spree, and a blow to Cadwalader, which has faced financial challenges and partner departures. The article discusses the implications for both firms and highlights Rule's high-profile client work and compensation at Cadwalader.

title: Best Places to Work: Intuit, Reno
summary: Intuit's Reno office, employing over 400 people, has been recognized multiple times as one of Northern Nevada’s Best Places to Work. The company focuses on financial software like QuickBooks and TurboTax, with the Reno site specializing in Intuit Payroll services. Intuit attributes its success in attracting talent to its recognition as a top workplace, offering various employee perks and demonstrating a strong commitment to community outreach.

title: Direxion Daily Technology Bull 3X Shares ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NYSEARCA:TECL)
summary: The Direxion Daily Technology Bull 3X Shares (TECL) ETF, launched in December 2008 and managed by Direxion, provides 3x leveraged exposure to the Technology Select Sector index, focusing on U.S. large-cap technology companies. title: Global X Autonomous & Electric Vehicles ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NASDAQ:DRIV)
summary: The Global X Autonomous & Electric Vehicles ETF (DRIV) invests in companies involved in autonomous and electric vehicles. The ETF was launched on April 13, 2018, and has $356.74 million in assets under management. Its top holdings include NVIDIA, Alphabet, and Tesla.

title: Sundar Pichai, Google - 10 Indian-origin CEOs 'ruling' the technology industry
summary: This article highlights 10 Indian-origin CEOs who lead major global technology companies, underscoring their significant impact on the industry. It details the careers and educational backgrounds of prominent figures such as Sundar Pichai of Google, Satya Nadella of Microsoft, and Shantanu Narayen of Adobe. The piece emphasizes the growing influence of Indian-origin leaders in the tech world.

title: Shantanu Narayen, Adobe - 10 Indian-origin CEOs 'ruling' the technology industry
summary: This article highlights 10 Indian-origin CEOs who hold leadership positions in major global technology companies, underscoring their significant impact on the industry. It details their backgrounds, career paths, and contributions to companies like Google, Microsoft, Adobe, and NetApp. The piece emphasizes the growing influence of Indian-origin executives in the global tech landscape.

title: HP unveils a new class of Windows 10 gaming devices
summary: HP has unveiled a new class of Windows 10 gaming devices, including the OMEN X Desktop, OMEN X by HP Curved Display, OMEN by HP with SteelSeries accessories, and the OMEN 17 Laptop. These new products are designed to provide the ultimate PC gaming experience, featuring advanced thermal management, powerful processors and graphics, and specialized accessories. The OMEN X Desktop offers full customization and will be available in configurations starting at $2,099.99 in October, while the OMEN 17 Laptop, priced from $1,599.99, focuses on portability and performance.

title: Cisco Systems to lay off about 14,000 employees: Report
summary: Cisco Systems is reportedly laying off about 14,000 employees, representing nearly 20 percent of its global workforce, as it transitions to a software-centric organization. This move follows similar job cuts by other major software companies like Microsoft and HP Inc this year. Cisco has been investing in new products such as data analytics software and cloud-based tools to offset sluggish spending in its traditional network hardware business.

title: Gartner Hype Cycle Highlights China's Aggressive Investment in High Tech Despite Economic Slowdown
summary: Despite an economic slowdown, China is aggressively investing in high technology, driven by government strategies and the need for business transformation. Gartner's 2016 Hype Cycle for ICT in China reveals rapid adoption of some technologies like cloud and digital commerce, while others like enterprise agile and smart city frameworks show evolving maturity. The report highlights significant opportunities in big data due to China's massive consumer base and government-backed "Internet Plus" strategy.

title: Technology Select Sector SPDR Fund ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NYSEARCA:XLK) $XLK
summary: This article provides comprehensive information on the Technology Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLK), an ETF tracking the Technology Select Sector Index. It details XLK's current price, key statistics, holdings, expenses, and recent news, noting its 30.6% increase this year. The fund offers concentrated exposure to technology companies within the S&P 500, with top holdings including NVIDIA, Apple, and Microsoft.

title: HP Inc.'s Omen X Design Seeks to Excite Buyer Interest in Desktop PCs
summary: HP's new Omen X desktop PC is designed to appeal to high-end users and DIY enthusiasts with its unique cube design, powerful graphics options, VR readiness, and full upgradability. The company is offering both pre-built systems and an empty shell for customization, as well as a partnership with Maingear for further personalization, starting at $1,800.

title: Assurant: transforming a risk management solutions business with Office 365
summary: Assurant, a global provider of specialty risk management solutions, has used Microsoft cloud technologies, specifically Office 365 and Microsoft Intune, to transform its business. This digital transformation has enabled real-time service demands, improved collaboration across its international offices, and enhanced mobility for employees while ensuring data security and regulatory compliance. The company leverages tools like SharePoint Online, Skype for Business Online, and Yammer to boost productivity, innovation, and internal communication.

title: G.E., the 124-Year-Old Software Start-Up (Published 2016)
summary: General Electric is undergoing a major transformation to become a top software company by 2020, investing heavily in its GE Digital division and developing an industrial operating system called Predix. This initiative aims to monetize the vast amounts of data generated by its industrial machinery, moving beyond traditional hardware sales to offering "business outcomes" and facing new competition from tech giants. The company is also striving to change its century-old engineering culture to embrace Silicon Valley's agile development practices.

title: Meg Whitman Rewinds Part of HP’s Inglorious Past With Software Sale
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) CEO Meg Whitman is divesting the company's software business to Micro Focus, marking a strategic move to slim down HPE and undo previous expensive acquisitions made by HP. This spin-merge, following another similar deal with CSC, aims to streamline HPE's operations and reduce its reliance on traditional hardware sales in a market increasingly dominated by cloud providers. The deal sees Micro Focus paying $2.5 billion to HPE, with HPE shareholders receiving $6.3 billion in the combined company's stock, making the new Micro Focus an entity with $4.5 billion in annual revenue.

title: HP Enterprise and Micro Focus deal to bring Autonomy back to the UK
summary: Micro Focus is acquiring a significant portion of Hewlett Packard Enterprise's non-core business in an $8.8 billion deal, which will result in the return of Autonomy, a British software firm, to the UK. This transaction brings Autonomy back after years of legal disputes between its former CEO Michael Lynch and HP regarding alleged misrepresentation of finances during its 2011 acquisition. The deal marks one of the largest for a British tech company in recent years.

title: Sarcos Robotics Secures Investment from Caterpillar, GE and Microsoft
summary: Sarcos Robotics has secured funding from strategic investors including Caterpillar Ventures, GE Ventures, and Microsoft Corporation, along with Cottonwood Technology Fund and other private investment firms. This capital injection will be used to expand the Sarcos team and accelerate the production and deployment of their Guardian line of robots, designed to improve safety and perform dangerous tasks across various industrial sectors. The investment also led to key appointments to Sarcos' board of directors, including Peter Klein, former CFO of Microsoft.

title: HP buys Samsung's $1bn printer business
summary: HP Inc. has acquired Samsung's printer business for $1 billion, aiming to revolutionize the $55 billion copier industry by integrating Samsung's laser printing technology and patents. This acquisition expands HP's presence in Asia and follows a recent move by HP's sister company, Hewlett Packard Enterprise, to sell its software business. The deal highlights HP's strategy to innovate in printing despite recent struggles for Samsung with its exploding Galaxy Note 7 phones.

title: Microsoft inks six-year deal with HP to use Dynamics CRM for sales and partnerships
summary: Microsoft has signed a six-year agreement with HP Inc. for the latter to use Microsoft's Dynamics CRM online service for direct sales and partnership tracking. This deal highlights Microsoft's continued growth in software-as-a-service (SaaS) and positions it against competitors like Salesforce and Oracle. HP already leverages Microsoft's Azure cloud and Office 365.

title: HP Buying Samsung Electronics' Printer Business for $1.05B
summary: HP is acquiring Samsung Electronics Co.'s printer business for $1.05 billion, marking its largest print acquisition to date. This deal aims to enhance HP's position in laser printing and expand into the multifunction printer market, leveraging Samsung's extensive printing patent portfolio. The acquisition is expected to close within a year and follows other significant business re-alignments for HP.
